messages.subject: inla.posterior.sample inaccuracy?
parts:
Hi, I'm trying to validate the samples generated with inla.posterior.sample. A simple independent Gaussian simulation gives me unbiased estimates as validated with 95% CI. However, a little bit more complicated Poisson AR(1) time-series example gives me underestimates. Could it be inaccuracy in INLA or perhaps a mistake in my code? Here is the parallelized code, where I first sample from AR(1) which gives expectation vector lambda to randomize from Poisson distribution, I fit the time-series with INLA Poisson AR(1) and check if the lambda vector falls within 95% and 50% CIs (should give around 95% and 50% but I got 81% and 41%):

library(INLA)
library(parallel)
library(doMC)
registerDoMC(cores=detectCores())
library(plyr)

n.t <- 20
n.posterior.samples <- 1000
n.iterations <- 1000

p <- ldply(1:n.iterations, function(i) {
  message("Iteration ", i)
  
  lambda <- exp(1 + arima.sim(model=list(ar=c(.7)), n=n.t))
  y <- rpois(n.t, lambda)
  data <- data.frame(y=y, t=1:n.t)
  
  result <- try(inla(y ~ 1 + f(t, model="ar1"), data=data, family="poisson", control.compute=list(config=TRUE)))
  if (inherits(result, "try-error")) return(NULL)
  samples <- inla.posterior.sample(n.posterior.samples, result)
  predictor <- exp(sapply(samples, function(x) x$latent[1:n.t,]))
  
  p95 <- 0
  p50 <- 0
  for (j in 1:n.t) {
    ci <- quantile(predictor[j,], c(.025, .975))
    p95 <- p95 + (ci[1] <= lambda[j] & ci[2] >= lambda[j])
    ci <- quantile(predictor[j,], c(.25, .75))
    p50 <- p50 + (ci[1] <= lambda[j] & ci[2] >= lambda[j])
  }
  
  return(data.frame(p95=p95, p50=p50))
}, .parallel=T)

mean(p$p95) / n.t # =0.81135
mean(p$p50) / n.t # =0.405

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.posterior.sample inaccuracy?
parts:
> result <- try(inla(y ~ 1 + f(t, model="ar1"), data=data,
> family="poisson", control.compute=list(config=TRUE)))
> if (inherits(result, "try-error")) return(NULL)
> samples <- inla.posterior.sample(n.posterior.samples, result)
> predictor <- exp(sapply(samples, function(x) x$latent[1:n.t,]))

The model contains an intercept parameter as well as the ar1 process,
but your posterior predictor only includes the ar1 part.
The predictor needs to include the sampled "fixed effect" as well.

Finn
